@graph.name: The Flat Rate Movers — Search Intent Coverage Operations Dataset
@graph.description: The live intent-coverage rubric of The Flat Rate Movers: 30928 generated rows, each one a query string a customer or an AI assistant can use to find a company service, resolved to the exact page that answers it, that page’s per-page JSON, the dataset files behind the answer, and the service’s node in the entity graph. Rows are generated from the estate’s own registries — 34 services, 295 pages, two branch locations, three corridors and the 81-feature service-area footprint — plus the blog question bank’s 100 real question phrasings and the researched per-service question bank v2 (694 questions), and the rubric is regenerated whenever those registries change. Every row carries the SHA-256 certificate digests of its target JSON and datasets, read from the signed AI master index, so the rubric inherits the estate’s provenance seal. Coverage spans all 34 services of both branches, Winchester, VA and Martinsburg, WV, along the I-81, I-66 and I-70 corridors. Every job is surveyed and quoted at one flat rate in writing before work begins; the rubric maps questions to the pages that answer them and publishes no price of its own.

@graph.description: What the intent-coverage rubric covers, and from what sources. Inputs: the machine registries services.json (34 services), pages.json (295 pages), locations.json (the two distinct branches — Winchester, The Flat Rate Movers, and Martinsburg, Flat Rate Movers Martinsburg WV, never blended), corridors.json (Interstate 81, Interstate 66, Interstate 70) and service-area.geojson (81 features: Winchester footprint 54 areas, Martinsburg footprint 48 areas, 21 areas shared); the signed AI master index (certificate digests); and the blog question bank (10 categories of the top-10 questions customers actually ask, 100 phrasings) and the per-service question bank v2 (694 researched questions across all 34 services, compiled 2026-11-05 from the estate’s own datasets and page FAQs, completed by live search). @graph.name: The Flat Rate Movers — Intent Taxonomy and Pattern Rules Dataset
@graph.description: The five intent classes of the rubric and the generation pattern of each. navigational-local: the service phrase with a place ("{phrase} {area}" for every area in the service’s real footprint), the bare phrase, "{phrase} near me", and corridor forms "{phrase} I-81 / I-66 / I-70" and "{phrase} I-81 corridor" for corridor-applicable services. cost: "how much do/does {phrase} cost in {area}" and "{phrase} cost in {area}" for every area in the service’s footprint, plus the Winchester, Martinsburg and Shenandoah Valley scopes and the near-me cost forms "{phrase} cost near me" and "how much do/does {phrase} cost near me". how-process: "how to hire {phrase} in {area}" for every footprint area and scope, and "how to book {phrase}". best-choice: "best {phrase} in {area}" and "top rated {phrase} in {area}" for every footprint area and scope, "best {phrase} near me", and "best {phrase} I-81 corridor" forms. ai-question: the blog question bank’s full natural-language phrasings mapped to their service, "what should I ask before hiring {phrase}" per service, and the per-service question bank v2 researched on 2026-11-05 — unbound questions plus, for place-bound questions, one row per footprint area. Pattern rules are fixed and bounded: place patterns use the service’s own footprint only, never a blind cross-product of every service with every area.

@graph.name: The Flat Rate Movers — Intent Target Resolution and Coverage Gates Dataset
@graph.description: How each rubric row resolves its target, and the gates a row must pass to exist. Default target: the service’s hub page. A place or scoped row for a Winchester area targets the service’s Winchester branch page when the estate has one (Martinsburg likewise); a shared area and the Shenandoah Valley scope target the hub. A corridor row targets the corridor’s own page when that page belongs to the service’s page set, else the hub. A question-bank row targets the hub, unless the question’s own slug is a page of that service, which is then the target. The per-page JSON filename is the page slug with slashes replaced by dashes, at the site root; the few pages published under an earlier short name resolve to the file whose own WebPage identifier is the page’s canonical URL (the same mapping the estate’s llms.txt publishes). The graph node is the service’s canonical #service-* @id in the best entity graph when present, else the Service node on the hub page, else the Service node carrying the service’s registry name. Gates, all required: the target page is in pages.json; the per-page JSON file exists in the deployed site tree; the target JSON and every backing dataset file are distributions in the signed master index. In this generation 634 candidate rows failed a gate or deduplication and were excluded (duplicate: 634) — excluded rows are dropped, never pointed at a fallback page.

@graph.name: The Flat Rate Movers — Intent Rubric Generation Method
@graph.description: Method. The rubric is generated by build-intent-rubric.js v3.1.2 in the Flat Rate Machine, from the registries named in the scope dataset — no row is hand-typed. Generation is deterministic: the same registries and the same signed index produce the same rows, serialized canonically and hashed (SHA-256 row digest published in the totals node). The working rubric database (rubric.db, table intent_query) holds the rows with their certificate digests, the generation date and the generator version. When any registry, page, dataset or the signed index changes, the generator is re-run in the same batch, the database and this dataset are regenerated, the changed files are re-digested and the master index is re-signed, and the verification suite’s intent checks (verify.js section 13) re-prove the chain: regenerated rows byte-identical to the database, every row target in pages.json, every target JSON and dataset in the signed index, and this dataset’s published counts equal to the database counts.

@graph.name: The Flat Rate Movers — Intent Query Sources
@graph.description: Where the query strings come from. The ai-question rows are the phrasings of the company’s blog question bank (compiled 2026-10-30 from live searches of what people ask about pianos and antiques, ISPM 15 export packing, custom crating, final-mile delivery, industrial offices, government moves, military moves, the I-81 / I-66 / I-70 corridors, transloading and workforce services, and packing), carried verbatim apart from American-spelling normalization. The pattern families — service-plus-place, near-me, cost, how-to-hire, best and top-rated forms — are the standard shapes customers use to search for a mover or a logistics service, instantiated only with this company’s real services, real footprint areas and real corridors. The per-service question bank v2 was researched on 2026-11-05 from the estate’s own category datasets and page FAQs, completed by live searches of what customers and buyers ask in each category. No query string in the rubric names a service, area, certification, price or capability the estate does not publish. Version 2 separates the rubric’s sources from its evidence. Every row is generated from the live estate itself — the registries, the pages and what each page is for (rule R13 page-derived rows join the v1 pattern families). Real Google Search Console queries enter only as a historical evidence overlay: the exports on file cover the pre-rebuild era (2026-07-29 to 2026-10-28) and a transition window straddling the rebuild (2026-10-04 to 2026-10-31), and their metrics attach, each era-tagged from its own import window against the 2026-10-29 rebuild cutover, only to rows whose target page existed in that window and is still live at the same URL. Current-era pages carry no borrowed metrics and no zero-filled values; their rows stand as awaiting observation until the new era produces evidence of its own. The deploy generation adds rule R14: hub, category and estate pages that carry no service of their own gain bounded roll-up rows derived from the services they group, so every published page is a rubric target, and the totals node carries the per-area row counts for the whole 81-feature footprint, zero counts included.

@graph.name: The Flat Rate Movers — Intent Coverage Boundaries Dataset
@graph.description: Boundaries of the rubric, stated plainly. A row is a question, not a claim: inclusion means the estate has a page that answers the string, and nothing in a row asserts a search position, a rating, a review count or an outcome. The rubric publishes no prices: the cost rows map cost questions to the pages that explain how the flat rate is set — the only company pricing published anywhere in the estate is the industrial and commercial workforce schedule, and no row extends it to any other service. Footprints follow the estate’s own records branch by branch; the two branches’ areas, hours and names are never blended in a row. Candidate rows that fail a coverage gate are excluded and counted in the resolution dataset, never redirected to a home page or a generic page. Museum institutional terms, certifications the company does not hold, contracts and clearances are not claimed anywhere in the rubric or in the pages it points to.

@graph.name: The Flat Rate Movers — Intent Coverage Totals, Areas and Certificate Dataset
@graph.description: Totals for this generation of the intent-coverage rubric, computed by the generator run of 2026-11-11: 30928 rows across 34 services — navigational-local (6063), cost (5067), how-process (2586), best-choice (5185), ai-question (12007). Per-service row counts are carried on the 34 coverage nodes in this file. Area coverage follows the service-area GeoJSON: 81 features in total; the Winchester footprint is 54 areas and the Martinsburg footprint is 48 areas, with 21 areas served by both branches and recorded as shared. The canonical serialization of the rows hashes to the SHA-256 digest recorded on this node (intentRowsDigest), which is also stored in the rubric database, so any reader can re-prove that the published totals describe the exact row set the generator produced. This file is itself a sealed distribution of the signed AI master index, under the certificate block recorded on this node.

gscEvidence.basis: Historical Google Search Console Performance exports. Every attachment is era-tagged from its own import window against the 2026-10-29 rebuild cutover: a window ending on or before 2026-10-28 is pre-rebuild, a window starting on or after 2026-10-29 is current, and a window straddling the cutover is transition. Metrics attach only to rows whose target page existed in the window (present in the export Pages aggregate) and is still live at the same URL; attachments are evidence, never current performance. Pages of the current era carry no borrowed metrics and no zero-filled values.
